claim: An agent was told to sign in and buy something. Someone watching should believe DemoKit carried out the whole purchase on a real store - logged in, put the item in the cart, filled the shipping form, and placed the order - and that it genuinely went through, because the last thing on screen is the store's own confirmation, not a checkmark DemoKit drew.
_ledger: S0  the store's sign-in page                                <- where the viewer starts
S1  signed in to the full catalogue                         <- type creds + Login
S2  the backpack in the cart, badge at 1                    <- add to cart
S3  the cart, ready to check out                            <- open the cart
S4  the shipping form, filled                               <- checkout + fill
S5  the order summary: line items, tax, total               <- continue
S6  the store's own 'Thank you for your order'             <- finish

steps.label: add the backpack
steps.shows: the button flip to Remove, the cart badge appear

steps.label: open the cart
steps.shows: the item in the cart, ready to check out

steps.label: fill the shipping form
steps.shows: name and postcode entered across the form

steps.label: review the order
steps.shows: the summary - line items, tax and the total

steps.label: place the order
steps.shows: the store's own confirmation - the order went through
